newsitem.title: USA: Cummins Engine 1996 sales set record.
newsitem.headline: Cummins Engine 1996 sales set record.

text.p: Cummins Engine Co said Wednesday its sales for 1996 set a record of $5.26 billion, up from $5.25 billion a year ago.

"We are pleased with our record sales for the year, despite a reduction in the North American heavy-duty truck market of more than 20 percent," Jim Henderson, chairman, said in a statement. "Sales for the fourth quarter equaled our former record in the second quarter of 1995, when demand from the North American heavy-duty truck market was at record levels."

Earlier, Cummins reported fourth quarter sales of $1.36 billion, up from $1.33 billion a year ago. It earned $1.03 a share in the fourth quarter, down from year-ago earnings of $1.05 that included a $76.0 million after-tax restructuring charge and a $68 million credit from the release of a tax valuation reserve.
For the year, it earned $4.01 a share, down from $5.52 in 1995 that included a $77.0 million restructuring charge.
Cummins said fourth quarter sales to the heavy-duty truck market were $270 million, 23 percent lower than the fourth quarter of 1995.
Sales of engines for the mid-range truck market were $134 million in the quarter, about flat with a year ago.
Power generation market sales were a record $362 million in the fourth quarter, up 18 percent.

In the bus and light commercial vehicles market, fourth quarter sales rose 12 percent to $208 million. Cummins said the increase was due to Chrysler Corp's Dodge Ram pickup truck. Cummins said 1996 engine sales for these trucks reached a record of more than 72,000 units, a 13 percent increase.
Sales to industrial markets of $242 million were $37 million higher than the fourth quarter of 1995.
